raw_response:
I'm 70 this year, been farming these 30 mu for 55 years. My two sons work at a factory in the county town, so they're only home for planting and harvest. My wife and I do the daily work, and my daughter-in-law helps when the grandchildren are in school.

We grow wheat and corn, same as everyone in our village. It's October now, time to plant the winter wheat.

**Wheat:** I watch my neighbor Lao Zhang — when he starts plowing, I start. I run the rotary tiller after the corn stalks are chopped and spread. For seed, I bought good improved seed three years ago and I've been saving it since. I'll plant about 12 kg per mu — no need to waste money buying new seed every year. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's 50 kg. Last spring the wheat looked a bit yellow at green-up, so I topdressed about 20 kg of urea per mu and it turned nice and green. This year I'll do the same — maybe a touch more, because Lao Li down the road always says better a little too much than too little. If the yield drops because of too little fertilizer, you lose more than the cost of the bag. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings don't freeze, once at jointing when the stems start growing, and once when the grain is filling. The electric pump costs about 15-20 yuan each time per mu, but dry wheat is no good. I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see aphids in spring I'll spray insecticide. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds — that's what I usually get.

**Corn:** The corn goes in right after wheat harvest in early June. There's no time to plow — maybe one light pass with the rotary tiller if I'm lucky, but usually we plant directly into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid corn seed every year from the seed shop, Denghai or something like that, costs about 55 yuan per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't work. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting. Then when the corn is knee-high, around big trumpet stage, I side-dress about 25 kg of urea per mu. Two irrigations for corn if the rain doesn't come — one at jointing and one at flowering. Weeds grow fast in summer, so I spray herbicide twice. If corn borer shows up, I'll spray insecticide. I expect about 500 kg per mu, same as last year.

My back isn't what it used to be, so I hire three or four people during harvest and the busy planting days — 150 yuan per day per person. The family does the rest: fertilizing, irrigating, spraying. All together, seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water, and hired help will cost me close to 20,000 yuan this year. That's a lot of money, but what can you do? I keep some cash aside for my wife's medicine and emergencies — can't put every yuan into the field.
